Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

hear verb

also hear about, hear of, can you hear me?, I hear that, catch (what someone says), I didn’t catch what you said

classical

Plaut. Aul. 269–270: tē vocō. ecquid audīs?
Cic. Sen. 21: nec vērō quemquam senem audīvī oblītum

audiō, audīre, audīvī, audītum

verb, fourth conjugation

hear; hear of, be told

With an accusative, an accusative and infinitive (audiō tē aegrōtāre, I hear you’re ill), dē and the ablative (hear about), and ex or ab for the person heard from. Audīn'?, for audīsne, is “Do you hear?”, “Listen!” (Ter.).

Other words

  • exaudiō, exaudīre, exaudīvī, exaudītum — hear clearly, catch (a sound)

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Epid. 239 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 287

    Nōn satis exaudiō: I can’t quite hear.

Examples

  • heus, Staphyla, tē vocō. ecquid audīs?

    Hey, Staphyla, I’m calling you. Do you hear me?Plaut. Aul. 269–270

  • Tacitus citius audiēs.

    You’ll hear it sooner if you keep quiet.Ter. Eun. 571

  • quod nec audieram ante nec vīderam, audīvī pariter et vīdī

    what I had neither heard of nor seen before, I heard of and saw at the same timePlin. Ep. 8.20.3

  • taedet jam audīre eadem mīliēns

    I’m sick of hearing the same thing a thousand times.Ter. Ph. 487

  • Nōn satis exaudiēbam quae loqueris.

    I didn’t catch what you’re saying.Traupman 95

  • nec satis exaudiēbam, nec sermōnis fallēbar tamen, quae loquerentur

    I couldn’t quite hear, and yet I didn’t miss what they were sayingPlaut. Epid. 2.2.55 (Lewis & Short s.v. exaudiō)

  • Nōn satis exaudiēbam dicta tua.

    I didn’t quite catch what you said.Traupman 287

See also listen carefully, I’m glad to hear it, understand, sense, learn.
